# ObiLabs Phishing — Design & Feature Spec (v0.1)

A working spec for the two-track, open-core phishing product built into Helios. Synthesizes the detection, simulation, add-on-UX, dashboard-IA, and differentiator research. Opinionated by design; MVP/later calls are explicit.

---

## Design stance (the five opinions that shape the build)

1. **One button, two rungs.** L1 and L2 are the *same* CardService/Apps Script engine — the difference is distribution, config, and trust, not capability. Build once.
2. **Stay in sensitive scopes forever.** Target `gmail.addons.current.message.action` (+ `script.external_request`). Never ship `gmail.readonly`/`gmail.modify` in the add-on → no CASA audit, a 3–5 day OAuth verification instead of an 8-week one, and a real trust story against KnowBe4's legacy "read, compose, send, permanently delete all your email."
3. **Injection is table stakes, not the headline.** KnowBe4 (DMI), Microsoft (native Direct Injection), Hoxhunt, SMARTFENSE, CanIPhish all inject via API. Sell **ownership + integration + no per-seat + explainability**, not novelty. `insert` is the default; `import`+`neverMarkSpam` is the "also test our filters" option.
4. **Directory-based impersonation is the real technical wedge.** Google already does the *coarse* version (employee-name spoof, OU-level, one action, no explanation, documented bypasses). Win on **report-time depth, explainability, directory-join accuracy, and org-wide rollup** — not on "we invented this."
5. **Deterministic-first, AI-optional; "indicators," never "verdicts"; non-punitive.** Show header-derived signals before any AI summary. Report-rate is the headline KPI, not a shaming click-rate. Honest degraded states everywhere (Mike's underpromise rule).

Naming used below: the **Phish Check** button (Track A) and **Phishing** module in Helios (both tracks live under one nav group with two sub-modules — Detection and Simulation — over a shared People/event substrate).

---

## 1. Recommended feature set, mapped to the ladder

### L1 — Copy-paste Apps Script button (open-source, unpublished)

| Feature | MVP | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Side-panel card add-on (CardService), Gmail desktop + mobile app | **MVP** | Card UI only — no toolbar button exists in the framework; design around the side panel. |
| On-demand "Check this email" action (`gmail.addons.current.message.action`) | **MVP** | Least-privilege, activates content access only on click. |
| Deterministic indicator engine (runs in the script, no backend needed) | **MVP** | Auth results from headers (SPF/DKIM/DMARC), From vs Reply-To mismatch, display-name vs address, freemail sender, lookalike/homoglyph domain, link-text vs href mismatch, urgency/keyword cues, first-time-sender heuristic. |
| Optional AI summary via BYO key (`script.external_request`) | **MVP** | User pastes their own key into the script constant. Opt-in enhancement, not the engine. |
| "Report" button → forward `.eml` + full headers to a configurable abuse mailbox / URL | **MVP** | Never mutate the mailbox from the add-on (incumbent pattern). |
| Output framed as "indicators found," colored rows (safe/suspicious/dangerous), 2–4 plain reasons | **MVP** | Underpromise: no "this email is safe." |
| Honest degraded state on AI/network failure ("couldn't reach analysis — here are the raw signals") | **MVP** | |
| Open-source repo: `.gs` + `appsscript.json` + README, install instructions, per-scope justification | **MVP** | The open-source-cred rung. |
| Homepage/help card with usage guidance | Later | |
| "I clicked / I entered credentials" self-report button (Hoxhunt pattern) | Later | Posts to the same abuse endpoint. |

### L2 — Marketplace add-on (free, published, verified)

| Feature | MVP | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Same engine, published via Workspace Marketplace SDK, verified publisher | **MVP** | Admin domain-wide / per-OU install → zero end-user consent friction (KnowBe4/Hoxhunt deploy this way). |
| **Admin config surface**: management URL (Helios endpoint), BYO AI API key, logo + name branding, confirmation text | **MVP** | The unoccupied slot: every incumbent add-on is a funnel into *its* cloud; this is bring-your-own-backend. |
| Simulation-aware "nice catch" (recognize own simulations, instant positive feedback) | **MVP when paired with L3/Track B** | Add-on asks the management URL "is this a known simulation?" against the Track B registry. Standalone (no Helios) falls back to a signed header marker in injected sims. |
| Per-verdict confirmation copy + org logo replaces ObiLabs mark | **MVP** | Within OAuth-consent + card-widget limits (can't restyle card chrome per tenant). |
| Multi-language confirmation strings | Later | Match Microsoft's up-to-7-languages bar. |
| Reporter gamification (score/streak, simulations only) | Later | |

**Review reality:** budget two manual gates before GA — OAuth verification (per-scope demo video; sensitive-only ≈ 3–5 working days) and a separate Marketplace app review (branding, naming, consent-screen consistency). No CASA because no restricted scopes.

### L3 — Helios Detection dashboard (paid, per-org, self-hosted)

| Feature | MVP | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Triage inbox** — report queue with disposition state machine: `Unknown → Clean / Spam / Threat / Simulation` | **MVP** | The core admin surface. Gmail native gives sub-Enterprise tenants *nothing* per-message; this is the fill. |
| Report ingestion (two paths): direct POST from the add-on management URL **and** DWD-watched abuse mailbox | **MVP** | Direct POST is low-latency; mailbox watch is the fallback and the path for Gmail-native reports. |
| **Directory-based internal-impersonation flag with explainable verdict** | **MVP** | The wedge — see §4.3. Runs at report time, so it can afford heavy per-message analysis an inline filter can't. |
| Clustering by sender / subject / URL / attachment hash | **MVP** | Group a campaign into one unit (Cofense/Abnormal/Material pattern). |
| Close-the-loop notify-reporter: per-verdict templated email with a plain-language summary variable | **MVP** | Copy Sublime's `asa_simple_summary` pattern; brandable, per-verdict. |
| Simulation auto-close (cross-check the Track B registry, resolve automatically) | **MVP** | Table stakes; every serious product does it. |
| Metrics: report volume, verdict mix, time-to-triage, top reporters, reporter reputation score | **MVP** | Reporter reputation from Cofense. |
| Remove-from-other-mailboxes (search + trash/label via DWD `gmail.modify`, reversible) | **MVP-lite** | Basic search-and-trash MVP; this is the one place L3 needs a restricted scope — self-hosted admin authorizes their own DWD, no Marketplace/CASA exposure. |

| RBAC (Security Admin / Auditor / Scoped Manager) | **MVP** | See §2. |
| Herd-immunity actions for other recipients (label/move; banners later — riskier, need message rewrite) | Later | Material/IRONSCALES pattern. |
| **PhishFlip**: turn a real reported phish into a Track B simulation template | Later | KnowBe4 feature; cheap once both tracks exist. |
| Community/crowd intel feed | Later | No network at launch. |

### Track B — Helios Simulation module (paid, per-org, self-hosted)

| Feature | MVP | Notes |
|---|---|---|

**Shared substrate (both tracks):** a single per-recipient **event stream**, the **People / Human-Risk** profiles, and the **Phish Check button** (a real report and a simulated report write to the same stream). The Track A button reporting a *real* phish must write into Track B's event model — otherwise real-reporter % is invisible.

## 2. Information architecture / layout (the two Helios modules)

**Nav placement.** Add one collapsible **Phishing** group to the Helios left module-nav (Lucide `shield-alert` for the group; purple `#8b5cf6` active state, consistent with existing modules). It expands to:

```
Phishing  (shield-alert)
├─ Overview                (layout-dashboard)   ← unified, both tracks
├─ Detection              (inbox)              ← Track A / L3 sub-module
│   ├─ Triage Inbox
│   ├─ Impersonation
│   └─ Settings
├─ Simulation             (send)               ← Track B sub-module
│   ├─ Campaigns
│   ├─ Templates
│   ├─ Landing Pages
│   ├─ Automations         (later)
│   └─ Settings
├─ People                 (users)              ← shared human-risk
└─ Reports                (file-text)          ← shared executive/board export
```

Pattern throughout (matches every mature product): **stat card → filtered table → entity detail**. Every card deep-links to a pre-filtered table; every table row opens a detail view. Column pickers, filter chips, search, CSV export with more columns than shown. Time-range selector defaults to last 6 months / last 5 campaigns.

### Overview (unified)
One screen of linked cards, no counts-only tiles — every headline is a ratio + 6-month sparkline:
- **Phish-prone %** (compromises ÷ delivered) with trend.
- **Report rate** (simulated) and **Real-threat reporters %** side by side.
- **Resilience ratio** (reports ÷ clicks) — the metric Hoxhunt/Proofpoint/Cofense headline instead of click rate.
- **Median time-to-click** and **median time-to-report (dwell)**.
- **Coverage** (% of users simulated in period).
- **Repeat clickers** count → opens the People list filtered.
- **Open triage items** (Unknown) → opens Triage Inbox.
- **Recent campaigns** table.
- **Impersonation hits this period**, by OU (the differentiator, on the home screen).

### Detection sub-module (Track A / L3)

**Triage Inbox** — the queue. Columns: reporter, reported-at, subject, sender, cluster size, **impersonation flag**, reporter-reputation, disposition. Disposition state machine `Unknown → Clean / Spam / Threat / Simulation`. Bulk actions on a cluster. Filter chips: Unknown, impersonation-flagged, external, has-attachment, simulation.

**Report detail** — opens a report:
- Rendered message + raw headers, `.eml` download.
- **Impersonation verdict panel** (the explainable string + signal breakdown, §4.3).
- Cluster panel (all matching reports, other recipients).
- Reporter panel (this user's reputation + history).
- Actions: set disposition; **Notify reporter** (per-verdict template with plain-language summary); **Remediate** (search-and-trash from other mailboxes via DWD); Flip to simulation (later).

**Impersonation** — a standing monitor (not just per-report). Table of directory-impersonation hits org-wide, grouped by OU/department, by pattern (display-name spoof / homoglyph domain / From≠Reply-To / freemail-VIP). This is the surface Google's native "Spoofing report" gestures at but never explains.

**Detection Settings** — button config (management URL, abuse mailbox, BYO AI key, branding), disposition auto-rules (confidence thresholds à la PhishER 95/75/65), notify-reporter templates, notification channels.

### Simulation sub-module (Track B)

**Campaigns** — list (status donut: sent/opened/clicked/submitted/reported) → **campaign detail**:
- Simulation-impact cards (compromised vs reported).
- All-user-activity table (delivered, opened, clicked, submitted, reported, deleted, replied, forwarded, out-of-office), filterable Compromised / Reported / Delivery-failed.
- First & average instance (first/avg click, first/avg credential entry).
- **Delivery-method badge** (Insert / Import) — makes the differentiator visible (§4.1).
- Per-recipient expandable timeline (UA/OS/browser/IP, **bot-click flagged**).
- CSV export carrying Department / Title / Manager / OU from the directory (free, because Helios owns it).

**Templates** — library (theme/difficulty/language filters) + HTML editor + preview + "send test to myself."

**Landing Pages** — built-in + custom + credential-harvest (values discarded) + coaching page editor.

**Simulation Settings** — delivery mode (Insert default / Import), spoof From identities, non-punitive defaults, scheduling defaults, bot-filter tuning.

### People (shared human-risk)
- Ranked lists on the page: **Repeat clickers** (risk) beside **Top reporters** (positive reinforcement) — Sophos pattern.
- Per-user profile: risk score, personal phish-prone %, full event timeline (simulated + real reports interleaved), training status. Repeat-clicker rule = consecutive-failure threshold (org setting, default 2, resets on pass) + a rolling "failed >N in 12 months" filter.

### Reports (shared)
Executive/board report as a **first-class templated object** (CISO + Security-Admin templates), PDF export, schedulable — so admins never rebuild slides (Hoxhunt's explicit dig at KnowBe4).

### RBAC (both modules)
- **Security Admin** — everything, org-wide by default.
- **Campaign Author** — templates/payloads/landing pages only, no reports (mirrors Microsoft's Attack Payload Author).
- **Auditor** — read-only (mirrors Security Reader).
- **Scoped Manager** — read-only for an OU / group / manager subtree (mirrors KnowBe4 Security Roles + Hoxhunt team dashboards).

Scoping is **additive on top of a shared org view** and derived from the directory, not from which admin connected OAuth. Critically, this scoping is **not gated behind a paid tier** (KnowBe4 puts Security Roles behind Advanced+).

## 3. Key UX flows

### 3.1 Phish Check button (report-button interaction)

1. User opens a suspicious email. Contextual trigger fires; the side-panel card shows a single primary action: **Check this email** (on-demand `message.action` keeps content access least-privilege).
2. On click → **loading card** ("Checking indicators…").
3. **Indicators card**: `DecoratedText` rows, one per fired signal, with a colored Lucide-style icon (green/amber/red hosted image URL — card chrome stays Google-styled, that's accepted). Header reads *"3 indicators found"*, never *"safe."* Rows e.g.: *"Reply-To differs from sender," "Sender domain is 1 character off yourdomain.com," "Link text says paypal.com but points to pay-secure.ru."*
4. **Optional AI summary** (BYO key): a short plain-language paragraph below the deterministic rows. If the AI call fails → the honest degraded state; deterministic rows still render.
5. **Next-step buttons** (one row): **Report** · **Learn more** (`OpenLink` to a guidance page or Helios) · optionally **I clicked** (later).
6. On **Report** → the add-on forwards the `.eml` + headers to the management URL / abuse mailbox (it does *not* mutate the mailbox), shows a confirmation card ("Reported to your security team"). 
7. **Simulation path**: if the management URL confirms this is a known Track B simulation, skip straight to an instant positive card — *"Nice catch. This was a security team test."* — and auto-close it in the L3 queue.

### 3.2 Simulation campaign-builder wizard

A 5-step wizard (Helios modal/side-sheet, purple primary, progress rail on the left):

1. **Name & objective** — campaign name, goal (baseline / training / targeted), non-punitive banner reminding the admin of coaching-first defaults.
2. **Template** — pick from library or clone/edit; live preview; difficulty/theme tags; "send test to myself."
3. **Audience** — pick from the live directory: whole org / OU / group / manager subtree. Shows resolved recipient count and department breakdown. No CSV.
4. **Landing & training** — choose landing page (incl. credential-harvest with values discarded) and the post-fail coaching page/micro-lesson.
5. **Delivery & schedule** — **this step makes differentiator #1 visible**:
   - Delivery mode toggle: **Insert (recommended)** vs **Import (also tests your filters)**, each with a one-line plain explanation and the honest caveat ("Insert bypasses your spam filter — it tests people, not defenses").
   - **From** field accepts any address with a live **spoof preview** of how the message will render in the inbox.
   - "No SMTP · no DNS · no allowlisting" affirmation badge.
   - Send window / spreading / timezone.
6. **Review & launch** — summary, recipient count, delivery method, a **dry-run** option (inject to admin only), then Launch. Post-launch redirects to campaign detail with the live donut.

### 3.3 Reports / triage dashboard flow

**Triage loop:** open the **Unknown** queue → open a report → read the **impersonation verdict** and **cluster** and **reporter reputation** in one panel → set disposition (`Clean/Spam/Threat/Simulation`) → **Notify reporter** with the per-verdict template (auto-fills the plain-language summary) → **Remediate** (search-and-trash the clustered message from other mailboxes via DWD) → the cluster resolves as one unit. Simulations auto-close without a human.

**Metrics reading:** land on Overview → a red/amber tile (e.g. resilience ratio down, or repeat-clicker spike) → click through to the pre-filtered People/Campaign table → export the executive PDF for the board. Every number is a ratio + trend + (later) benchmark line, never a bare count.

---

## 4. Making the three differentiators visible

### 4.1 Gmail-injection delivery — sell ownership, not novelty
- **In the wizard** (§3.2 step 5): the Insert/Import toggle, the any-From spoof preview, and the "no SMTP / no DNS / no allowlist" badge are the visible payoff. Competitors bury the delivery method; we foreground it.
- **On campaign detail**: a persistent **delivery-method badge** (Insert / Import).
- **In setup**: a one-time "Authorize injection" step (Super Admin grants DWD once) contrasted against the SMTP-relay + SPF/DKIM/DMARC + allowlist gauntlet GoPhish and SMTP tools demand. Reuse the existing Helios `googleScopesForPath` per-call minting to grant **only** `gmail.insert` at injection time.
- **Honesty as a feature**: surface the caveat in-product — "Injected messages bypass your filters. Switch to Import mode to also test whether your defenses would have caught this." This is the Import+`neverMarkSpam` upsell *and* the underpromise rule.
- **Beat KnowBe4's seam**: KnowBe4 DMI still needs allowlisting for the *training* follow-up emails. Inject both the lure and the follow-up — and say so.

### 4.2 Org-wide visibility — re-scoped so it survives a KnowBe4-aware buyer
- **Drop** the "competitors silo each admin like a separate tenant" line — false against KnowBe4/Defender/Hoxhunt. It is true against **GoPhish** (siloed per login, no cross-admin visibility — long-standing open issues) and **Google-native** (aggregate-only, reporters not even identified) and **lightweight Marketplace add-ons**. Point the claim there.
- **The real, honest pitch**: "directory-native shared org view + RBAC, self-hosted, no per-seat tax, zero re-onboarding." Make it visible via:
  - A **scope selector** (whole org / OU / group) any Security Admin sees on Overview and People — the shared surface is the default, scoping is opt-in.
  - An RBAC settings page showing delegated roles that **mirror the org's actual Workspace roles/OUs**; a new sub-admin inherits the shared view instantly (no second OAuth, no separate tenant).
  - Directory-derived department/manager/OU roll-ups on every table (free because Helios owns the directory) — the concrete thing GoPhish and Google-native cannot produce.

### 4.3 Directory-based internal-impersonation — the strongest genuine wedge
Position **above** Google's native protection (coarse OU-level on/off, one action, no user explanation, documented bypasses). Win on report-time depth + explainability + directory-join + rollup.

- **Signal set** (superset of Google's binary check), computed at report time and on inbound sim/real analysis:
  - Display-name **exact + fuzzy** match against the live directory (all users, aliases, groups).
  - **IDN/homoglyph normalization + Levenshtein** distance of From/Reply-To domain vs owned domains *and* directory.
  - **From ≠ Reply-To** mismatch (and three-way From/Reply-To/impersonated-brand mismatch, Ironscales pattern).
  - **First-time external sender**; freemail + employee-name; recently-registered Reply-To lookalike.
  - **VIP/exec targeting** (from the org chart).
  - Auth results (SPF/DKIM/DMARC) as **context, never the sole gate** — auth validates the domain, never the free-text display name.
- **Make it visible three ways:**
  1. **Explainable verdict string** in the triage report panel, e.g. *"Display name 'Jane Okafor, CFO' matches a directory VIP, but From = `jane.okafor@0kafor-corp.com` — a homoglyph of yourdomain.com; Reply-To routes to a domain registered 4 days ago."*
  2. **Same explanation to the end user** in the Phish Check card at report time — report-time depth an inline filter can't afford.
  3. **Org-wide rollup** on the Impersonation page, by OU/pattern — which impersonation patterns hit which departments.
- **Directory as ground truth** is the unfair advantage: Helios already holds the authoritative employee/VIP/domain/alias list, so this is a cheap, accurate join an external gateway can only guess at.

---

## 5. Open questions / risks to resolve before building

**Scopes, auth, and injection**
1. **`gmail.insert` over DWD is a buyer security-review flag** and a known abuse target (Unit 42). Confirm the authorize flow (Super Admin, one-time) and that minting is strictly per-call — it must **never** enter `REQUIRED_SCOPES` (DWD all-or-nothing would blanket-401 every connected workspace, per the documented Helios gotcha).
2. **Insert vs Import default and the realism caveat.** Insert bypasses filters → tests people only, and inserted mail has no `Authentication-Results`/`Received` chain (a savvy user or downstream tool can tell it was injected). Decide the default (recommend Insert) and how loudly to surface the tell.
3. **Remove-from-other-mailboxes needs `gmail.modify` (restricted).** Self-hosted sidesteps CASA, but confirm reversibility and the justification copy for the admin.

**Add-on / L2**
4. **BYO AI key handling + prompt-injection.** Where is the key stored (add-on config vs Helios)? The analyzed message is **attacker-controlled** — the AI prompt must treat it as data, not instructions, and we must decide whether content leaves the org (BYO endpoint) or routes through Helios. Data-residency implications.
5. **L2 review timeline and per-tenant branding limits.** Two manual gates (OAuth verification + Marketplace review); card chrome can't be restyled per tenant — set expectations.
6. **Simulation-awareness without Helios.** How does a standalone L2 recognize its own simulations with no management URL? (Signed header marker in injected sims + a fallback confirmation string.)

**Ingestion & data**
7. **Report ingestion path, latency, dedup.** Direct POST from the add-on vs DWD-watched abuse mailbox — pick the primary, define dedup when both fire, and how Gmail-native reports (up to 4h alert-center delay) are reconciled.
8. **Bot/scanner false-click filtering accuracy.** Even with internal injection, Google/M365 link-scanning and mobile link previews can fire. Define the telltale thresholds and be transparent about discounting.
9. **Multi-domain orgs and aliases** in impersonation matching — confirm all owned domains + aliases feed the homoglyph/Levenshtein set.

**Simulation program**
10. **Landing-page hosting + credential-capture ethics/legality.** Helios must serve public landing pages; credential-harvest must discard values; simulations against employees may need HR/works-council/GDPR sign-off (esp. EU). Define consent and non-punitive policy defaults up front — punitive programs suppress real reporting.
11. **Training content: build vs partner.** v1 links to a coaching page; the full micro-learning/LMS is a later build-or-partner decision.
12. **Benchmark cold-start.** No network data at launch — do not ship a fake industry benchmark; label trend-vs-own-baseline until data exists.

**Positioning**
13. **Pin the org-wide referent.** The differentiator must name its target (cross-admin-within-org / GoPhish / Google-native / Marketplace add-ons), never a blanket "everyone silos" that a KnowBe4-aware buyer rejects on sight.
